narrative.overview:
The artifact at the centre of this product is the ledger kept at the club's front desk: every sale a line, every member a page, and a slip torn off and handed over with each entry. The interface is that ledger made electronic for a laptop — ruled, compact, unembarrassed about being full of figures — and the slip is still real: a Khmer receipt with a QR code that the gate reads. Where NAN HR's register tracks days and hours, this one tracks entries and dollars, and it inherits the same near-monochrome slate register to do it.

Two things distinguish it from its siblings. First, the scale: the reference screen is a 1366×768 laptop at a counter with a queue, so controls are 32px, the content pane pads at 12px, and tables have a compact "ledger" density tuned line by line for Khmer. Second, the colour: the club has three facilities — swim, gym, steam — and a combination package, and each has a colour that staff read faster than a name. Blue, green, orange and purple are the ledger's index tabs, used on ticket tiles, price rows and chips, and they are the only saturated system beyond the four record-state marks.

The type system is built for Khmer first: Roboto and Nokora bundled offline, secondary text darkened until it clears 6.5:1 on white, and a caption step with a taller line so stacked Khmer consonants never touch. On paper the same care becomes a HarfBuzz-shaped Noto Sans Khmer on 80mm thermal roll.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled, not boxed — hairline dividers and a wash band do the separating work
Compact by design: a 32px control scale and a ledger table density for a laptop
Four facility colours as index tabs, four record-state marks, nothing else saturated
Khmer-tuned contrast and line height, on screen and on the printed slip
One amber mark, on the sign-in surface only — the family mark, not the club's
Flat at rest, sticky header, offcanvas sidebar with an icon rail

rules.name: The Facility Rule
rules.body: Blue, green, orange and purple mean swim, gym, steam and combination — on a ticket tile, a price row, a chip, a report column. They are never chosen per page for variety. The three duplicate palettes in `Ticket.tsx`, `TicketPriceConfig.tsx` and `MemberPriceTable.tsx` (one of which reads a `badge` key that does not exist) are drift to collapse into one definition.

rules.name: The Four Marks Rule
rules.body: Success, Warning, Info and Stop are the complete state palette. A new record state maps onto one of them or is expressed in ink and annotation grey.

rules.name: The Grey Ledger Rule
rules.body: Chrome is Floor and Paper. The two hundred raw `gray-*` and ninety `black` classes in the pages are the same drift NAN HR had: new work uses `bg-card`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`, and a page touched for other reasons is the moment to convert.

rules.name: The Legible Khmer Rule
rules.body: Annotation Grey stays at 38% lightness. Lightening it back toward shadcn's default for Latin taste breaks Khmer at caption size, and the detector currently finds no grey-on-colour defects here — keep it that way.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the family's sign-in surface and nothing inside the app. It is not a heading, a button variant, a chip or a "this looks plain" fix.

rules.name: The Palette Restraint Rule
rules.body: No gradients on data surfaces. The indigo gradient on the member profile header and the purple-to-pink banner and purple heading in the customer-type report are the three "AI palette" findings the detector raises today; they are drift, and a report tile is Paper with a facility chip.

rules.name: The Dark Mirror Rule
rules.body: Every token has a `.dark` counterpart, and thirty- four `dark:` utilities exist, but nothing enables dark mode and a stray `.dark { @apply bg-gray-800 }` conflicts with the token. The app is light-only in practice; do not design for dark here until the toggle exists.

rules.name: The Locked Pairing Rule
rules.body: Roboto and Nokora are a binding pair. Roboto is flagged by the design detector as an overused face and that flag is knowingly suppressed in `.impeccable/config.json`: the Khmer metric match outranks Latin distinctiveness in a product whose fallback language is Khmer. A proposal to change the Latin face must prove compatibility with Nokora in a compact table row and on the printed slip.

rules.name: The Khmer-In-Every-Stack Rule
rules.body: Every stack carries a Khmer face — the global rule guarantees it on screen. The print window's `Khmer OS Content` should become Nokora so paper and screen shape Khmer the same way.

rules.name: The Caption Floor Rule
rules.body: `text-caption` (12px at 1.6) is the small step. Arbitrary `text-[12px]`, `text-[10px]` and `text-[9px]` sizes are drift except on the printed slips, which are paper, not chrome, and are recorded in `.impeccable/config.json`.

rules.name: The Black Price Rule
rules.body: Black weight is for the price on a ticket tile. Six uses today, all of them that; a seventh anywhere else is a defect.

rules.name: The Laptop Rule
rules.body: Design at 1366×768. Thirty-two-pixel controls, twelve-pixel page padding, compact table density. A component that only works at 1920 is wrong here.

rules.name: The One Card Rule
rules.body: Every list, CRUD and report route is one Card with one title and one DataTable. Nested cards are how a dense page becomes an unreadable page.

rules.name: The Two Densities Rule
rules.body: A table is either comfortable (uppercase tracked caption headers, zebra rows, `py-1.5`) or compact (the Notion-style ledger: `text-caption` headers in sentence case, `py-[3px]` rows at `17px` leading, tabular figures, vertical hairlines, no zebra). The choice is made per table in `tableDensity.ts`, never per cell.

rules.name: The Column Priority Rule
rules.body: Narrow screens drop columns by importance or stack the row as a card; they never wrap figures.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: If it does not float, it has no shadow. Cards and table shells get `border border-border`.

rules.name: The Scrim-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Dialog separation is the `bg-black/80` scrim's job; reach for it before a heavier shadow.

rules.name: The One Rule Weight Rule
rules.body: 1px, `{colors.rule}`, everywhere on screen except the ticket tile's facility edge.

rules.name: The Radius Ladder Rule
rules.body: Controls 6px, tables and dialogs 8px, cards and tiles 12px, chips full. A container never rounds tighter than the control inside it.

rules.name: The Slip Rule
rules.body: The printed slip has square corners, a 2px black frame, black text on white and 2px rules. It is paper: no radius, no grey, no tint that a thermal printer would fade.

rules.name: The Confirming Motion Rule
rules.body: No entrance animation on a table row or a tile, no attention-seeking loop, no bouncy easing. This is an eight-hour tool.

rules.name: The Keyframe Home Rule
rules.body: Keyframes live in `tailwind.config.cjs` or `index.css`. `animate-shimmer`, `animate-fade`, `animate-slide`, `animate-step-in` and `animate-fadeIn` are used but defined nowhere — they do nothing today. Define them in the config or remove the classes.

dos: colour a ticket tile, price row or chip by its facility — swim blue, gym green, steam orange, combo purple — from one shared definition.
map a record's state onto Success, Warning, Info or Stop, and use the matching button variant for the action that produces it.
keep controls at `32px` and page padding at `12px`; this is a laptop tool.
pick a table's density once, in `tableDensity.ts`, and set every money and count column in Figure with `tabular-nums`, right-aligned.
keep Annotation Grey at 38% lightness and `text-caption` at 1.6 line height; check a Khmer header cell before calling a table done.
give resting cards and table shells `border border-border` and no shadow; reserve shadow for the sticky header, dialogs and dropdowns.
keep the printed slip black on white with square corners and 2px rules.
use the token classes (`bg-card`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`) instead of `gray-*` and `black` on new work.
reach for a shadcn primitive in `frontend/src/components/ui/` before writing one, and delete `_ui-backup-pre-nanhr/` rather than consulting it.
donts: use a gradient on a data surface; the profile header and the customer-type banner are the drift the detector already names.
define a facility palette in a page; three copies exist and one reads a key that is not there.
use black weight anywhere but the price on a ticket tile.
use an arbitrary `text-[Npx]` size on screen; `text-caption` is the floor and the slip is the only exception.
add a fifth saturated hue outside the four facilities and four marks; purple belongs to combination packages, not to headings.
use amber inside the app; it is the sign-in mark.
put a thick or coloured border on a card; the ticket tile's facility edge is the one exception.
use an animation class that has no keyframe, or declare a keyframe inside a page.
design for dark mode until a toggle exists and the stray `.dark` rule is removed.
introduce a fifth icon library; four already coexist (Heroicons, Lucide, react-icons, Headless UI). Lucide is the shadcn default; converge on it.
let a table wrap or shrink its figures on narrow screens; drop columns by priority or stack the row.
